These Criminal Petitions have been filed by the petitioners/accused Nos.6 and 7 respectively seeking to quash the proceedings in PRC No.12 of 2025 on the file of the Additional Judicial First Class Magistrate at Bhuvanagiri, for the offences under Sections 420, 406, 464, 468, 471, 286, 336 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860, (for short, 'the IPC'), Section 9(B)(1)(b) of the Explosives Act, 1884 and Sections 4 and 5 of the Explosive Substances Act, 1908.

entities.text: Additional Judicial First Class Magistrate at Bhuvanagiri
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. Heard Mr. K.Rajashekar, learned counsel for the petitioners, and Mr. Jithender Rao Veeramalla,
learned Additional Public Prosecutor, appearing on behalf of respondent-State.
3. Learned counsel for the petitioners submitted that the issue raised in the present criminal petitions is squarely covered by the orders passed by this Court in Crl.P.No.3913 of 2025, dated 25.10.2025, where under accused Nos.8 to 10 have approached this Court seeking to quash the very same proceedings in PRC No.12 of 2025 on the file of the learned Additional Judicial Magistrate of First Class at Bhuvanagiri and this Court allowed the said Criminal Petition and quashed the proceedings against them and also placed copy of the said order.
The petitioners are also entitled for the very same relief on the ground that the very same allegations are levelled against them.

Hence,
continuation of the proceedings against the petitioners is a clear abuse of the process of law.

sentences.text: The said submission has not disputed by the learned Additional Public Prosecutor.

5. In view of the above said submissions and taking into consideration the orders passed by this Court in Crl.P.No.3913 of 2025, dated 25.10.2025, this Court finds it to be a fit case to exercise jurisdiction under Section 528 of the BNSS to quash the proceedings against the petitioners herein.

6. Accordingly, both the Criminal Petitions are allowed and the proceedings in PRC No.12 of 2025 on the file of Additional Judicial First Class Magistrate at Bhuvanagiri, against the petitioners/accused Nos.6 and 7, are hereby quashed.
